title: Any authenticated staff can read and write all service bookings via PostgREST
description: The application treats `driver_management` and `service_booking` as separate modules, but Row Level Security on `service_bookings` grants every authenticated user unrestricted SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE. A staff member without module permission can still query customer PII and mutate bookings using only the published anon key and their own JWT.
root_cause: Policy `service_bookings_all_auth` uses `USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)` for the `authenticated` role.
intended_behavior: Staff without `driver_management` or related module grants should not access `service_bookings` rows through the Supabase API.

trace.description: Page loads rows with `supabase.from('service_bookings').select(...)` under the staff JWT.
`service_bookings_all_auth` permits any authenticated principal all operations on the table.

evidence.description: CREATE POLICY service_bookings_all_auth ON public.service_bookings TO authenticated USING (true) WITH CHECK (true);
Staff modules come from `get_all_my_permissions()` but are not enforced at the table layer for bookings.

conditions.description: Attacker holds any valid staff Supabase Auth session (not admin-only).
Publishable anon key and project URL are available to clients (standard SPA/mobile deployment).

execution.attacker_perspective: Authenticated staff user who was not granted `driver_management`.
instructions: In a local Supabase stack seeded with two staff users, grant `service_advisor` permissions only to user A (no driver_management).
Sign in as user A and call the REST path above with the Authorization header set to user A's access JWT and apikey set to the anon key.
Compare result row count with user B who has explicit driver_management; user A should still receive rows if this policy is unchanged.
execution.observed_result: PostgREST returns booking rows for user A despite missing module permission in `user_module_permissions`.

remediation.strategy: Replace the blanket authenticated policy with module- or role-aware RLS (e.g. `has_module_view('driver_management')` OR admin), or route all booking access through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that enforce the same checks used in the UI.

likelihood.reason: Any active staff account can use browser devtools or a REST client; no module gap required beyond valid login.

impact.reason: Exposure and tampering of customer contact data, addresses, pickup/drop details, and booking workflow for the entire dealership.

confidence.reason: Policy text and grants are explicit in the baseline migration; no later migration tightens `service_bookings` RLS.

title: SECURITY DEFINER get_permissions_for_user lacks caller authorization
description: The function comment states only admins may call it, but the SQL body selects permissions for arbitrary `target_user_id` with no `auth.uid()` or `is_admin()` guard. It is granted to `anon` and `authenticated`, so unauthenticated or non-admin callers can enumerate another user's effective modules.
root_cause: SECURITY DEFINER function omits an admin check while ACLs expose it to `anon`.
intended_behavior: Only active admin users may read another user's module permission rows (used for impersonation/admin tooling).

trace.description: Function selects from `user_module_permissions` for supplied UUID with no caller check.
GRANT ALL ON FUNCTION get_permissions_for_user TO anon, authenticated.

evidence.description: Comment '-- Only admin users may call this' is not enforced in SQL.
WHERE clause filters on `p.user_id = target_user_id` only.

conditions.description: Caller may be anonymous (anon key) or any authenticated staff user.
Attacker knows or guesses a target user's UUID (visible in many staff-facing tables).

execution.attacker_perspective: Non-admin staff or anonymous API client with the publishable key.
instructions: POST to `/rest/v1/rpc/get_permissions_for_user` with apikey set to the project anon key and Authorization set to Bearer <anon key> or a non-admin staff JWT.
Supply a known staff user UUID in the JSON body.
Inspect JSON response for module names and capability flags.
execution.observed_result: Permission rows for the target user are returned without verifying the caller is admin.

remediation.strategy: Add `IF NOT public.is_admin() THEN RAISE EXCEPTION ...` (or equivalent) at the start of the function; revoke EXECUTE from `anon`; keep authenticated only if needed.

likelihood.reason: Requires anon or staff API access and a target UUID, both commonly available in this app model.

impact.reason: Discloses internal authorization layout and aids targeted abuse of other gaps; does not directly exfiltrate customer job data by itself.

confidence.reason: Function body and grants are unambiguous in source; no corrective migration found.

title: booking-source-sync Edge Function has no request authentication
description: `supabase/config.toml` sets `verify_jwt = false` for `booking-source-sync`, and the handler performs no shared-secret or admin check before using service-role clients to read a source database and write into `all_service_data` on the target project.
root_cause: Publicly invokable Edge entrypoint with service-role credentials and no caller authentication.
intended_behavior: Only scheduled cron or trusted operators should trigger cross-database booking sync.

trace.description: POST handler proceeds without Authorization validation.
Creates Supabase clients with `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and optional source service key, then mutates target data.

evidence.description: Only method check; no auth helper such as `validateRequest`.
Documents intentional `verify_jwt = false` for cron—does not add an alternative shared-secret gate in code.

conditions.description: Deployed function URL is reachable with the publishable anon key (default Supabase Edge deployment).

execution.attacker_perspective: Internet client with the project anon key only.
instructions: POST to the deployed `booking-source-sync` function URL with headers `apikey: <anon>` and `Authorization: Bearer <anon>`.
Send a small batch dry-run body and observe JSON sync statistics in the response.
execution.observed_result: Function executes sync logic using service-role credentials without rejecting the caller.

remediation.strategy: Require a high-entropy cron secret header, enable JWT verification with a dedicated service user, or restrict invocation to Supabase scheduled triggers only; never run service-role sync on an unauthenticated HTTP surface.

likelihood.reason: Requires knowledge of the function URL and anon key, both embedded in client apps or infra configs.

impact.reason: Unauthorized sync or resync can corrupt or flood `all_service_data`, affecting customer comms, reminders, and downstream workflows.

confidence.reason: Config and handler lack auth in source; pattern matches other hardening notes in repo docs for different functions.

title: Customer portal authenticates with phone number as both identifier and password
description: `customer_start_session` accepts the same last-10-digit value for username and password, granting a 12-hour session token. Rate limiting (10 attempts per 15 minutes per phone key) reduces brute force but does not add a second factor.
claimed_root_cause: Password check `v_user <> v_pass` is skipped in favor of equality of two phone-derived fields.

trace.description: Login compares last-10-digit username and password.
Issues 64-byte random session token on success.

evidence.description: IF v_user IS NULL OR v_pass IS NULL OR v_user <> v_pass THEN RAISE EXCEPTION.
Brute-force cap: 10 attempts per 15 minutes per phone_key.

blockers: Business acceptance of phone-only customer login and monitoring for abuse is a deployment/operations decision not visible in code.

validation_plan.local: Model account takeover attempts under the rate limit in a local stack; measure whether operators accept residual risk for vehicle owners.
validation_plan.deployment: Review customer fraud incidents and optional OTP step without probing production accounts.

title: Several report/sync Edge Functions disable JWT verification
description: Besides `booking-source-sync`, `config.toml` sets `verify_jwt = false` on earnings reports, insurance telecalling, and similar jobs. Some handlers use `_shared/auth.ts`; others may rely solely on network obscurity.
claimed_root_cause: Cron-oriented functions disable platform JWT verification without a uniform in-code secret or service-role caller check.

trace.description: Multiple `verify_jwt = false` entries for report and sync functions.
Imports `validateRequest`—auth strength depends on implementation not fully traced for every sibling function in this pass.

blockers: Per-function handler review and deployed Supabase invocation policies were not exhaustively verified in this run.

validation_plan.local: For each `verify_jwt = false` function, confirm either validateRequest/admin gate or cron secret before service-role work.
validation_plan.deployment: Inventory scheduled triggers vs public HTTP routes in Supabase dashboard.

title: Claimed universal Driver Management access via service_booking module
description: Prior builds allegedly auto-added `driver_management` when staff had `service_booking`. Current `src/App.tsx` maps `/driver-management` to `['driver_management','admin']` only and does not add `driver_management` in `loadAccess` for non-admins.
claimed_root_cause: Implicit module expansion in `loadAccess` for service_booking users.

trace.description: Driver route requires explicit module or admin.

evidence.description: No service_booking alias on driver-management route.

reason: Issue is remediated at the reviewed commit. Residual impact for bookings is superseded by confirmed RLS gap on `service_bookings` (any authenticated staff already has API access).
